jesus_calms_storm.setting: A boat on the Sea of Galilee, evening
jesus_calms_storm.conflict: A violent storm threatens to capsize the boat while Jesus sleeps
jesus_calms_storm.turning_point: Jesus wakes and speaks to the wind and waves, and they obey
jesus_calms_storm.theme: Trust in the midst of fear
jesus_calms_storm.sensory_atmosphere: dark water, strong wind, crashing waves, rocking boat, sudden stillness
jesus_calms_storm.passageFinalLine: They were exceedingly afraid, and said to one another, 'Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?'

woman_at_well.setting: Jacob's well near the town of Sychar, midday
woman_at_well.conflict: A woman draws water alone at noon, avoiding others; a Jewish stranger asks her for a drink
woman_at_well.turning_point: Jesus reveals he knows her past, and offers living water that never runs dry
woman_at_well.sensory_atmosphere: bright midday sun, dry dust, stone well, cool water, quiet road
woman_at_well.passageFinalLine: Jesus said to her, 'I am he, the one who speaks to you.'

road_to_emmaus.setting: The road from Jerusalem to Emmaus, late afternoon
road_to_emmaus.conflict: Two grieving disciples walk away from Jerusalem, crushed by the crucifixion
road_to_emmaus.turning_point: A stranger walks with them, explains the scriptures, and is recognized when he breaks bread
road_to_emmaus.sensory_atmosphere: dusty road, fading sunlight, quiet footsteps, warm lamplight at table, broken bread
road_to_emmaus.passageFinalLine: They related the things that happened along the way, and how he was recognized by them in the breaking of the bread.

lost_sheep.conflict: One sheep wanders away from the flock of ninety-nine
lost_sheep.turning_point: The shepherd leaves the flock to search and finds the lost sheep
lost_sheep.theme: Every one matters and is worth finding
lost_sheep.sensory_atmosphere: open grass, rocky terrain, bleating, wind across the hills, warm wool
lost_sheep.passageFinalLine: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.

daniel_lions_den.setting: The royal court of Babylon and the lions' den
daniel_lions_den.conflict: Officials trap Daniel with a law forbidding prayer to anyone but the king
daniel_lions_den.turning_point: Daniel is thrown to the lions but God shuts their mouths; he emerges unharmed
daniel_lions_den.sensory_atmosphere: stone palace, sealed pit, growling lions, cold night air, morning light
daniel_lions_den.passageFinalLine: So this Daniel prospered in the reign of Darius, and in the reign of Cyrus the Persian.

samuel_listens.conflict: A young boy hears a voice calling in the night but does not know who speaks
samuel_listens.turning_point: Eli recognizes the voice as God's and teaches Samuel to answer
samuel_listens.sensory_atmosphere: warm lamplight, hushed room, soft nighttime stillness, a voice in the dark
samuel_listens.passageFinalLine: Yahweh revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by Yahweh's word.

queen_esther.conflict: A decree threatens to destroy Esther's people; approaching the king uninvited risks death
queen_esther.turning_point: Esther risks her life to speak, and the king extends his scepter
queen_esther.theme: Courage for such a time as this
queen_esther.sensory_atmosphere: gold throne room, heavy curtains, silent courtyard, held breath, extended scepter
queen_esther.passageFinalLine: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king's wrath was pacified.

rest_for_the_weary.setting: An open gathering place in Galilee
rest_for_the_weary.conflict: People carry heavy burdens of labor, law, and exhaustion
rest_for_the_weary.turning_point: Jesus invites them to lay down their burdens and take his yoke instead
rest_for_the_weary.sensory_atmosphere: warm afternoon, tired bodies, dusty sandals, gentle voice, easing shoulders
rest_for_the_weary.passageFinalLine: For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.

elijah_at_horeb.setting: A cave on Mount Horeb, the mountain of God
elijah_at_horeb.conflict: Elijah hides in a cave, terrified and alone, believing he is the last faithful one left
elijah_at_horeb.turning_point: God passes by — not in the wind, earthquake, or fire, but in a still small voice
elijah_at_horeb.theme: God meets us in our lowest moments, not with force but with gentleness
elijah_at_horeb.sensory_atmosphere: dark cave mouth, howling wind, shaking ground, roaring fire, then sudden quiet whisper
elijah_at_horeb.passageFinalLine: Yet I reserved seven thousand in Israel, all the knees which have not bowed to Baal, and every mouth which has not kissed him.

david_and_goliath.setting: The Valley of Elah between the Israelite and Philistine camps
david_and_goliath.conflict: A giant champion challenges Israel daily and no soldier dares answer
david_and_goliath.turning_point: A shepherd boy steps forward with a sling and five stones, and the giant falls
david_and_goliath.theme: Courage comes not from size or armor but from trust in God
david_and_goliath.sensory_atmosphere: wide valley, morning mist, clinking armor, shouting armies, a single smooth stone, silence after the fall
david_and_goliath.passageFinalLine: David took the head of the Philistine and brought it to Jerusalem, but he put his armor in his tent.

mary_and_martha.conflict: Martha is distracted by preparations and frustrated that Mary sits listening instead of helping
mary_and_martha.turning_point: Jesus gently tells Martha that Mary has chosen the better portion, which will not be taken away
mary_and_martha.theme: Presence over productivity; stillness is not laziness
mary_and_martha.sensory_atmosphere: warm kitchen, clattering dishes, fragrant bread, quiet room, seated at feet, gentle voice
mary_and_martha.passageFinalLine: Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.

ruth_and_naomi.setting: The road from Moab to Bethlehem
ruth_and_naomi.conflict: Three widows face destitution; Naomi urges her daughters-in-law to go back to their families
ruth_and_naomi.turning_point: Ruth refuses to leave, declaring 'Where you go I will go; your people shall be my people'
ruth_and_naomi.theme: Loyalty and love that chooses hardship over comfort
ruth_and_naomi.sensory_atmosphere: dusty road, distant hills, tearful goodbye, two women walking together, empty fields ahead
ruth_and_naomi.passageFinalLine: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her, who returned out of the country of Moab. They came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

hagar_in_wilderness.conflict: Cast out with her son, Hagar's water runs out and she places her child under a bush to die
hagar_in_wilderness.turning_point: God hears the boy crying, opens Hagar's eyes, and she sees a well of water
hagar_in_wilderness.theme: God sees the forgotten and provides in the wilderness
hagar_in_wilderness.sensory_atmosphere: scorching sand, empty waterskin, a child crying, shade of a bush, sudden glint of water
hagar_in_wilderness.passageFinalLine: He lived in the wilderness of Paran. His mother got a wife for him out of the land of Egypt.

prodigal_son.setting: A family estate, then a far country, then home again
prodigal_son.conflict: A son demands his inheritance, wastes it in a far country, and ends up feeding pigs
prodigal_son.turning_point: The starving son decides to return home, and his father sees him from far off and runs to embrace him
prodigal_son.theme: No distance is too far for a father's love to reach
prodigal_son.sensory_atmosphere: rich feast, then empty fields, pig stench, torn clothes, dusty road home, running footsteps, warm embrace, music and celebration
prodigal_son.passageFinalLine: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.

joseph_interprets_pharaohs_dreams.conflict: Pharaoh is troubled by two dreams no one can interpret; a forgotten prisoner is remembered
joseph_interprets_pharaohs_dreams.turning_point: Joseph interprets the dreams as seven years of plenty followed by seven years of famine, and Pharaoh puts him in charge
joseph_interprets_pharaohs_dreams.theme: Faithfulness in forgotten seasons prepares you for the moment that matters
joseph_interprets_pharaohs_dreams.sensory_atmosphere: prison darkness, then bright throne room, golden court, troubled king, calm voice, signet ring placed on a hand
joseph_interprets_pharaohs_dreams.passageFinalLine: Pharaoh said to Joseph, 'See, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.'

moses_and_jethro.setting: The Israelite camp in the wilderness
moses_and_jethro.conflict: Moses judges disputes from morning until evening, exhausting himself while the people wait in long lines
moses_and_jethro.turning_point: Jethro says 'What you are doing is not good' and counsels Moses to appoint others to share the burden
moses_and_jethro.theme: Wise rest is not weakness — carrying everything alone will wear you out
moses_and_jethro.sensory_atmosphere: long lines of waiting people, hot sun, tired voice, an elder's firm counsel, relief as others step forward
moses_and_jethro.passageFinalLine: Moses let his father-in-law depart, and he went his way into his own land.
